considered.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity is literally output per unit of the capital that produced it: gross profit net of capital consumption, measured against a capital base that includes the firm's self-built knowledge stock alongside its recorded assets, so a firm scores high only if its research has translated into product-market surplus rather than into an expanding expense line.
considered.reasoning: This drops the cash-flow numerator that made the previous version a relabelled cash-based operating profitability and instead places the intangible capital where it belongs — in the denominator as productive capital — so the score falls, not rises, for firms that spend heavily on research without converting it into margin. The gen-0 attempt at this concept failed only because it used a five-year trend on a degenerate R&D-only denominator (coverage 0.060); the level form with an assets-plus-knowledge base is well conditioned for every firm and should run near 0.14 coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Funded Without Equity Dilution
considered.hypothesis: Research programs financed by repeatedly issuing equity transfer value away from existing holders and signal that internal economics do not support the program, whereas the same research intensity sustained without dilution reflects a self-financing innovator; the difference in book equity growth not explained by retained earnings is the dilution channel.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the flagged operator sweep, this introduces the one financing dimension the archive has never touched — external equity — after cash flow, working capital, total leverage and debt maturity have all been tested, and it is measured as a five-year cumulative issuance rate so it captures a financing regime rather than a single-year event. The interaction is essential: dilution is uninformative for firms with no research program to finance, and research intensity is uninformative without knowing who paid for it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net Durable Intangible Capital Behind a Cash-Earnings Floor
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), dlc))), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm's net durable intangible capital — knowledge built, less premium purchased, less debt falling due — is only credible when cash earnings never collapsed in the past five years, and both components can be measured from the income statement and balance sheet for the full sample.
considered.reasoning: Net Durable Intangible Capital produced the archive's highest FF5 t-statistic (ls_talpha 4.51, alpha 4.8%) at coverage 0.145 but an almost flat cross-sectional slope (1.69), while the cash-earnings floor produced a solid slope (2.93) with alpha 3.8% at the same coverage; the joint construct targets the missing dimension of each without reverting to the coverage-limited oancf history. This is the batch's leading candidate for a final signal that is simultaneously broad, precise in alpha, and monotone in the cross-section.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor
considered.hypothesis: Firms should be judged on how they allocated intangible investment over a common horizon: five years of research spending against five years of additions to purchased intangibles, so a legacy goodwill balance inherited from the 1990s neither helps nor hurts, and only live allocation decisions count.
considered.reasoning: Gen 6 showed that the flow version of the intangibles penalty is as informative as the stock version (recent deal flow fmb 4.78 versus stock fmb 4.59) and that same-period buy-versus-build comparisons carry a strong negative slope (fmb −4.50), but the archived leader still nets a five-year research flow against a lifetime intangible stock — a horizon mismatch. Aligning both legs to five-year flows keeps the winning economics while removing a stale-balance-sheet component that should mechanically add noise and turnover.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Worst-Year Productivity of Knowledge-Augmented Capital
considered.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity means the capital base including self-built knowledge earned a solid product-market surplus even in its worst year; the level of that productivity is a cyclical reading, but its five-year floor identifies franchises whose knowledge capital genuinely works.
considered.reasoning: The level version of this productivity ratio delivered a respectable slope (fmb 3.47) but weak alpha (1.5%, ls_talpha 1.72), the mirror image of the continuous constructs whose alphas are strong and slopes weak, which suggests its top decile mixes genuinely productive franchises with firms enjoying a good year. Taking the floor inside the ratio — the transformation that lifted the penalized-capital construct to fmb 4.19 — tests whether downside durability is what converts a productivity measure into an alpha-bearing one, and it does so without adding a second ranked leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deal Premium Measured in Years of Cash Flow
considered.hypothesis: The burden of purchased intangibles should be denominated in the firm's own cash generation, not in assets: a goodwill balance equal to one year of operating cash flow is a routine bolt-on, whereas one equal to a decade of cash flow is an unrecoverable premium, and the market prices the assets-scaled version but not the cash-denominated one.
considered.reasoning: Rather than re-pairing two archived legs under MIN, this fuses the intangibles penalty and the cash-generation requirement inside one bounded ratio in which the two themes interact multiplicatively — a firm is penalised only to the extent its deal premium is large *relative to* five years of realized cash flow. The bounded form avoids the explosive denominators that killed earlier yield constructs, and continuous specifications of this family have produced the archive's highest FF5 t-statistics while the cash-flow content should supply the cross-sectional slope those constructs lacked.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance Penalty Concentrated in Researchers
considered.hypothesis: External equity financing is not uniformly bad: issuing shares to fund a research program that the business cannot yet support is value-destroying, whereas the same issuance by a firm with no research program carries far less information, so the issuance penalty should be concentrated among research-intensive firms and reverse sign there.
considered.reasoning: The gen-6 dilution conjunction produced the archive's largest Fama-MacBeth slope (6.50) with no tradable alpha, which is what happens when a MIN kink places the informative firms in the middle of the score distribution rather than in the extreme deciles; the centered-gate structure instead puts self-funded researchers at one tail and dilutive researchers at the other, with non-researchers neutral, and that structure has repeatedly converted strong slopes into FF5 alpha in this archive. The proposal is a state-dependence test of a known effect rather than an additive blend of two anomalies, which is precisely the distinction the critic drew.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Post-Deal Cash Delivery of Acquirers
considered.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5), at), 0.05), SUB(IND_RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), LAG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), 5))), 0.5))
considered.hypothesis: The market's penalty on purchased intangibles should apply only to deals that failed to deliver: among firms that materially expanded their intangible book over the last five years, those whose cash-flow margin has actually risen since bought real cash-generating assets, while those whose margin fell bought future impairments.
considered.reasoning: This is an event-time delivery test rather than a profitability sort on a subsample: the conditioning variable is a five-year intangible expansion and the ranked variable is the cash-flow change measured over exactly that window, so the score asks whether the deals worked, a question no archived signal poses. It matters for the final consolidation because every winning signal so far penalises purchased intangibles unconditionally, and if delivery separates good from bad acquirers then the unconditional penalty is leaving a large, cleanly identified long side on the table.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Acquisitive Expansion Without an Earnings Floor
considered.hypothesis: The clean short position is the firm that spent five years enlarging its purchased intangible base while never establishing a cash-earnings floor: the balance sheet grew in unverifiable assets exactly where operating performance failed to support them.
considered.reasoning: The archive's two best short-side results — the buy-versus-build conjunction (fmb −4.50, alpha −3.2%) and the impairment overhang (alpha −3.9%, ls_talpha −3.42) — each achieved only one of slope or alpha, and both were constrained either by the oancf history or by a one-sided kink. Pairing the five-year acquisitive flow with the negated income-statement floor gives a well-populated short leg at roughly 0.14 coverage and provides the short-side counterpart to Signal 1 for the final round.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Freshness of the Knowledge Stock
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge capital depreciates fast, so what matters is vintage: a firm whose current-year research is a large share of its five-year cumulative research has a live, growing program, while a low share means the stock is stale and its embedded productivity is already in prices.
considered.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg measures the size or origin of the knowledge stock, never its age, yet an economics of obsolescence implies two firms with identical R&D-to-assets differ sharply if one is ramping and the other is winding down — and the ratio is self-normalising, so it is free of the size and industry tilts that R&D intensity carries. This is the batch's exploratory slot; it uses raw xrd so that non-reporters are excluded rather than mislabelled as stale, at the cost of coverage near 0.05.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Never-Heavy Purchased Intangible Balance Sheet
considered.hypothesis: The current purchased-intangible balance is contaminated by survivorship: a firm that just impaired its goodwill looks intangible-light today precisely because the deal failed, so the honest measure is the worst (highest) intangible burden the firm carried over five years, and only firms that were never heavy deserve the credibility premium.
considered.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg reads the current stock or the recent flow, both of which mechanically reward firms that wrote intangibles off, which is exactly the population the impairment story says should be penalised; the five-year maximum removes that contamination and is a new economic correction rather than a recombination. Pairing it with the income-statement cash-earnings floor keeps coverage near 0.14, and if the alpha rises relative to the current-stock version we learn the archive's leading result has been diluted by post-impairment firms sitting in the long leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deal Premium in Years of Gross Profit
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The payback horizon of a firm's purchased intangibles is best expressed in years of gross profit — the surplus actually available to recover a deal premium — and a premium that would take many years of gross profit to earn back is unrecoverable regardless of how small it looks against total assets.
considered.reasoning: This keeps the cash-denomination insight that produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.505) while replacing the fragile five-year cumulative operating cash flow denominator, which can be negative or near zero and would rank distressed cash-burners at the top, with gross profit, which is positive for virtually every operating firm and therefore monotone. Conjoining with the cash-earnings floor supplies the cross-sectional dispersion the standalone cash-denominated measure lacked (fmb −0.08) and holds coverage near 0.14 rather than the 0.09 of oancf-based versions.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Lightness with Stable Cash Margins
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), revt), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The economic story specifies stable cash flows, and the right stability measure is the variability of the cash margin a firm earns on each dollar of revenue — a product-market property — rather than the variability of cash flow scaled by assets, which mixes margin stability with balance-sheet composition.
considered.reasoning: The asset-scaled volatility version worked (alpha 4.0%, fmb 3.28) but was restricted to coverage 0.081 by the oancf history, whereas the cash-margin version is computable from the income statement for the full sample and isolates operating predictability from leverage and asset intensity. It replaces an uninformative ablation with the one second-moment channel the archive has not tested, and it directly discriminates whether "stability" in the mandated story is a margin phenomenon or a balance-sheet phenomenon.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Worst-Year Return on Capital Charged for Deal Outlays
considered.expression: IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5))), 5))
considered.hypothesis: A firm should be charged for the cash it actually committed to buying intangible capital during the measurement window, so the capital base is assets plus the five years of purchased-intangible additions, and the test is whether pre-research cash earnings cleared that base even in the worst year.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the arbitrary double-charging of the legacy intangible stock — inherited unexamined from the parent construct — with a principled charge equal to the deal outlays made inside the same five-year window over which the floor is computed, so numerator and denominator refer to one consistent period. It is a single-leg construct with no rank splice, buildable from the income statement and balance sheet at roughly 0.14 coverage, and it isolates whether the acquisitiveness penalty works through the capital base of a productivity ratio rather than as a separate ranked screen.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), MA(revt, 3))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The build-versus-buy allocation should be judged against the size of the business it serves, not against the asset base, because asset scaling mechanically favours asset-light firms and conflates the intangible allocation decision with capital intensity.
considered.reasoning: Every intangibles leg in the archive is scaled by assets, so the recurring result could partly reflect an asset-light tilt rather than an allocation choice; revenue scaling breaks that link while leaving the economic content — five years of research spending net of five years of purchased-intangible additions — unchanged. Paired with the income-statement cash-earnings floor it also runs at roughly 0.13 coverage rather than 0.084, so a comparable alpha would show the effect is neither an asset-scaling artefact nor a post-1988 sample artefact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit-Funded Knowledge Stock
considered.hypothesis: Research dollars spent in profitable years are credible investment; research dollars spent in loss years are subsidised experimentation, so the priced knowledge stock is the cumulative research a firm financed while actually earning money, not its total research spending.
considered.reasoning: This puts the quality-intangibles interaction inside the accumulation itself — each year's research is admitted to the stock only if that year's earnings were positive — rather than conjoining a research measure with a separate profitability screen, which is a construction the archive has never used and which cannot be produced by ranking R&D intensity and profitability separately. It is a single continuous leg with no rank splice, computable for the full sample at roughly 0.145 coverage, and the smooth form is the one that has generated the archive's highest FF5 t-statistics.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The durability condition should be competitive rather than absolute: a firm qualifies if it out-earned its industry peers even in its worst year, which identifies a firm-specific moat supporting the research program rather than membership of a structurally profitable industry.
considered.reasoning: The industry-demeaned floor was tested only once, in gen 3, where it held up against the raw floor (fmb 4.24, alpha 3.8%, Sharpe 0.371) but was paired with a plain R&D-intensity leg and limited to the oancf sample; here it is combined with the strongest intangibles leg and the income-statement cash-earnings measure, extending it to roughly 0.13 coverage. This closes the run's central identification question — whether the repeated result is a moat effect or a residual industry-composition effect — while remaining a plausible top performer in its own right.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Build Minus Buy with Worst-Year Cash Flow After Research
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The binding condition for a research program is not that cash flow was positive but that cash flow was large enough to pay the research bill in the worst year: a firm whose operating cash flow net of research spending never went negative has an unconditionally self-financing innovation program.
considered.reasoning: This is not a re-pairing of two archived legs because the quality gate itself now contains the intangibles variable — research spending is deducted from cash flow before the floor is taken — so the interaction operates inside both legs rather than only across them, and heavy researchers must clear a proportionately higher bar. The gen-2 attempt at self-funding used a count of qualifying years and failed on portfolio evidence (alpha −0.9%), whereas the magnitude form at the worst-year floor has never been tested and preserves the dispersion that a 0–5 count destroys.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit-Funded Research Under an Acquisitiveness Constraint
considered.hypothesis: Two independent conditions define durable intangible productivity: research must have been financed out of profitable years, and the firm must not have been simultaneously buying intangible assets from outside; whichever condition binds determines the firm's credibility.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the unit-for-unit netting with a weakest-link conjunction removes the arbitrary weighting the critic identified, since neither channel is forced onto the other's dollar scale and each enters as a separate constraint. The profit-weighted accumulation is the genuinely new element — the earnings test is applied year by year inside the knowledge stock rather than as a separate screen — and pairing it with the validated five-year acquisitiveness penalty keeps coverage near 0.14 with no cash-flow-statement requirement.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deal Outlays and Maturing Debt in Excess of Equity
considered.hypothesis: A firm is fragile when its recent purchases of unverifiable intangible assets plus the debt maturing within the year exceed the book equity available to absorb an impairment, and the excess — not the ratio — is the economically meaningful quantity.
considered.reasoning: Putting the equity cushion in the numerator as a subtraction and scaling everything by assets removes the sign pathology the critic identified: negative-equity firms now score at the fragile extreme rather than at the safe one, and the measure is monotone and defined for every firm. It follows the construction that already worked on the short side (the gen-5 impairment overhang, alpha −3.9% with ls_talpha −3.42) while adding the two elements that overhang omitted — recent deal outlays and near-term maturities — which the archive has separately shown to carry short-side information.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Cash-Flow-Backed Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is a plain rank-product of two long-published anomalies (R&D-to-assets intensity à la Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis and cash-based profitability à la Novy-Marx/Ball et al.) with no gating or conditioning structure, so it is essentially a double-sort screen whose loading will be dominated by the profitability leg rather than any genuine interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Earnings-Stability-Deflated Intangible Intensity
critic_notes.rationale: The two quantities have incommensurate units, so the ratio is mechanically dominated by the near-zero-volatility denominator (1/VOL blows up), meaning the signal will largely rediscover the known low-earnings-volatility/low-fundamental-risk premium rather than test intangible credibility, and a single winsorization pass will not fix that scaling pathology.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual-Validated Intangible Expansion
critic_notes.rationale: The quality leg is literally the negated Sloan (1996) total-accruals measure and the intangibles leg is close to the asset-growth/investment anomaly, so the product is a repackaging of two canonical anomalies whose expected positive sign will most plausibly be delivered by the accrual leg alone.

critic_notes.target_name: Durable Intangible Productivity Trend
critic_notes.rationale: The trend in gross profit per dollar of R&D-plus-booked intangible capital is a genuinely non-standard construct rather than a relabeled known anomaly, though the reviewer should watch coverage loss from zero-intangible denominators and note that SUMRANK is additive and therefore weights, rather than truly gates, the stability channel claimed in the hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Solvency-Gated R&D Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The oancf/(dltt+dlc) gate divides by zero for debt-free firms, dropping exactly the safest self-funded innovators the hypothesis is about, and the arbitrary 0.5 threshold plus a [0,1] IND_RANK multiplier makes the sign flip depend on an unmotivated cut point with a large near-zero dead zone for low-R&D firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Low-Quality Intangible Balance-Sheet Inflation
critic_notes.rationale: The short-side framing is coherent and the assets-scaled goodwill/intangible change avoids the degenerate-base problem, but the mechanism overlaps heavily with documented acquirer/goodwill-impairment underperformance and the quality leg is again accruals plus earnings volatility, so the negative slope is likely a rediscovery rather than a new interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Short-Horizon Weakest-Link Funded Research
critic_notes.rationale: This is a pure lookback-window tweak (5→3 years) of the archived gen-0 winner with no new economic content, and the stated coverage motivation is likely wrong since the binding sample constraint in that signal is the oancf history requirement that this variant only marginally relaxes while COALESCE already makes the R&D leg universal.

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Intensity with Margin Floor
critic_notes.rationale: The swap from a cash-flow floor to a downside net-margin floor is a genuinely different economic channel (product-market durability vs. funding capacity) and the income-statement alignment of both legs is well-argued, though the components individually flirt with known R&D-to-sales and earnings-stability/quality anomalies so the novelty rests entirely on the weakest-link conjunction.

critic_notes.target_name: Internally Funded Intangible Build
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archived Externally Financed Intangible Build with the funding leg sign-flipped and re-centered using the 0.5-subtraction trick already deployed in another archived gen-0 signal, and the stated mechanics are inconsistent — because the build leg is an uncentered IND_RANK, firms scored near zero are the largest intangible *shrinkers*, not the "no build" firms the reasoning claims are neutralized.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Share of Capital Renewal
critic_notes.rationale: The bounded intangible-vs-depreciation composition ratio is a legitimately new and scale-free construct that is not a simple restatement of R&D-to-assets, but the claimed coverage improvement is unfounded since the retained five-year oancf floor (plus a new dp requirement) remains the binding sample constraint.

critic_notes.target_name: Triple-Constraint Durable Innovator
critic_notes.rationale: Nesting MIN over the legs of two already-archived positive signals is mechanical stacking rather than a new mechanism, and since the added retained-earnings leg is monotone in the same quality direction it will mostly just shrink the long portfolio to firms already selected by the existing weakest-link signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Liquidity-Buffered Research Commitment
critic_notes.rationale: Substituting a balance-sheet slack stock for the cash-flow flow floor is a clean one-factor discrimination between two competing interpretations of the gen-0 result and should genuinely expand coverage, though net-working-capital-to-assets overlaps with known working-capital and financial-constraint effects, so the test hinges on the conjunction outperforming its legs.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Yield on Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The materiality-indicator × centered-rank structure is a legitimate reuse of the archive's best-performing template applied to a genuinely new variable, but note the ranked quantity (operating cash flow per dollar of cumulative R&D) mechanically favors the *least* R&D-intensive firms within the material group and is heavily loaded on plain profitability, so it may test the opposite tilt from the "research franchise" story in the hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-Year Total Liquidity Floor on Research
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical merge of the two archived quality legs into one term that sums an annual flow (oancf) with a balance-sheet stock (act−lct) in incompatible units, and since net working capital is typically much larger it will be dominated by the already-tested working-capital version rather than constituting a distinct economic construct.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The organic-versus-acquired intangible contrast is a genuinely new leg and the quality leg is held fixed for a clean one-change comparison, though the netted variable mixes two incompatible measurement bases (expensed cumulative R&D vs. deal-priced book intangibles) and risks being a repackaged bundle of the known R&D-to-assets and goodwill/acquisitiveness anomalies.

critic_notes.target_name: Funded Research Ramp
critic_notes.rationale: Internally inconsistent — the R&D-change leg is an uncentered IND_RANK in [0,1], so the score's sign is determined entirely by the cash-flow rank and firms with no research-intensity change do *not* sit near zero as the reasoning claims, leaving a signal that is mostly a profitability sort scaled by ramp rank, with a huge tie mass at zero change for non-reporters.

critic_notes.target_name: Research-Capitalized Earnings Floor
critic_notes.rationale: Economically well-motivated but this is the fourth instance of the same MIN(R&D-intensity, worst-year-profitability-floor) template in the archive (Weakest-Link, Margin Floor, Hidden Gap), so the R&D add-back and capitalized denominator amount to a cosmetic re-specification of an already-explored design rather than a substantively different mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Booked-Intangible Heaviness in Cash-Flow Drawdown
critic_notes.rationale: Conditioning the drawdown construct on booked-intangible heaviness is a new and coherent subpopulation restriction with a clear impairment-cliff mechanism and a two-sided, well-labeled spread, though the drawdown leg is close to a profitability-deterioration proxy and the diagnostic value hinges on the 20% threshold not shrinking the effective sample too far.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquired-Intangible-Light Cash Floor
critic_notes.rationale: A clean, internally consistent ablation of the gen-2 leader that isolates the goodwill-penalty leg, but as a standalone signal it reduces to "asset-light balance sheet + high worst-year cash-flow profitability," which is close to well-known intangible-heaviness/goodwill-impairment and cash-based-profitability effects, so its value is diagnostic rather than novel.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Intangible Tilt with Working-Capital Buffer
critic_notes.rationale: This is a one-leg substitution that mechanically splices the archive's two highest-alpha components, and since the liquidity leg already produced a collapsed Fama-MacBeth slope (t=1.41) in its own conjunction, the most likely outcome is a cosmetic re-run of the leader with a diluted cross-sectional slope rather than a substantively different mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Brand Capital with Cash-Flow Floor
critic_notes.rationale: COALESCE(xad,0) turns the large population of non-reporters of advertising expense into apparent zero-brand-capital firms that the MIN operator will systematically place in the short leg, so the "brand vs. knowledge capital" test is confounded with a disclosure-selection artifact, and the underlying advertising-intensity effect is itself a published anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Goodwill-Heavy Firms Split by Cash-Flow Floor
critic_notes.rationale: Inside a fixed subpopulation the signal is just a centered rank of worst-year cash-flow-to-assets, i.e., a direct restatement of the cash-based profitability anomaly on a subsample, and without a contrast against the non-goodwill-heavy group the proposal cannot identify the interaction it claims to test.

critic_notes.target_name: Marginal Earnings Return on Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The expression correctly implements the stated marginal-return concept (three-year change in smoothed earnings per dollar of accumulated R&D, gated to material researchers and centered for a two-sided spread), it addresses a specific identified flaw in the gen-2 Cash Yield signal, and the denominator is bounded away from zero by the gate; the main residual risk is overlap with the known profitability-growth effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Research on a Tangible, Unlevered Balance Sheet
critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent and a defensible one-design-choice contrast against the Weakest-Link signal, but tangible-net-worth-less-debt is likely highly collinear with the already-tested retained-earnings-less-debt gate (alpha only 2.1%) and with book leverage generally, so the expected incremental information is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Rank-Space Organic Versus Acquired Intangibles
critic_notes.rationale: This is a third algebraic parameterization of the same two ingredients already tested in the archive (dollar-netted organic-minus-acquired at fmb 5.08 and the goodwill-light ablation at fmb 4.59), paired with the identical unchanged cash-flow floor, so it is a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a new mechanism — and since SUMRANK already equalizes scale, wrapping it in IND_RANK adds little beyond what the two archived legs jointly reveal.

critic_notes.target_name: Average Versus Worst-Case Cash Backing of Intangible-Light Firms
critic_notes.rationale: A single-operator ablation (TS_MIN over 5y → MA over 3y) of the archived "Acquired-Intangible-Light Cash Floor" is a legitimate and honestly framed diagnostic, but it is a cosmetic variant of an existing signal rather than a substantively different construct, and its likely outcome — that a mean cash-profitability screen works about as well on more firms — mostly restates the well-known profitability premium.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Capital Share of Knowledge Plus Obligations
critic_notes.rationale: The construct is internally consistent, bounded, high-coverage and genuinely distinct from the archive's conjunction family, but it is a monotone transform of R&D-stock-to-liabilities and therefore sits close to the well-documented R&D-intensity and low-leverage effects, so the incremental content over a simple rescaling of a known anomaly is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt-Financed Goodwill Overhang
critic_notes.rationale: The expression and negative expected sign are coherent (MIN is high only in the goodwill-heavy/high-leverage quadrant) and the balance-sheet-only design gives a well-populated short leg, but the target population is essentially "recent leveraged acquirers," which overlaps materially with the published acquirer-underperformance, asset-growth and net-operating-asset anomalies, so any result will need to be shown to survive those controls.

critic_notes.target_name: Patient-Capital Research Commitment
critic_notes.rationale: Debt maturity is a genuinely untested dimension in this archive and is the financing attribute most directly mismatched with a research program's payoff horizon, the MIN/rank construction matches the stated conditional hypothesis, and the expected positive sign follows naturally — though the claimed high coverage is overstated since the five-year R&D stock, not dlc, is the binding constraint (~0.09).

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Capital Per Tangible Asset with Cash Floor
critic_notes.rationale: The expression contradicts its own hypothesis: dividing by (at − gdwl − intan) means a large purchased-intangible balance *shrinks the denominator and raises* the score, so goodwill-heavy firms are rewarded rather than penalized — the opposite of the stated "not padded with purchased intangibles" intent and of the archived organic-minus-acquired result it claims to re-express.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Intangible Tilt on Short-Dated Debt
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical MIN-splice of two legs that already exist verbatim in the archive (the gen-2 organic-minus-acquired numerator and the gen-4 NEG(dlc/at) gate), so it is a cosmetic leg swap rather than a new economic mechanism, and the coverage gain it advertises comes only from dropping the cash-floor requirement that was arguably doing the work.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-Year Coverage of Near-Term Claims
critic_notes.rationale: Redefining the floor as a genuine coverage ratio (cash flow against claims due) rather than an asset-scaled level is a defensible, economically distinct change to the most-repeated archive component, though the denominator ADD(dlc, lct) double-counts short-term debt since dlc is already inside current liabilities, and the intangible-light leg is still lifted unchanged from gen-3.

critic_notes.target_name: Purchased Intangibles in Excess of Liquid Resources
critic_notes.rationale: The construct (operating intangible assets minus net working capital, scaled by assets) is a partial re-derivation of net operating assets, a well-known published anomaly, and internally the two components pull against each other — NOA evidence says high working capital predicts *low* returns, whereas here subtracting it pushes the score toward the predicted-high-return end, so a flat slope is a plausible mechanical outcome rather than a diagnostic one.

critic_notes.target_name: Research Backed by Cash Unit Economics
critic_notes.rationale: The critique of ib/revt being mechanically depressed by expensed R&D is correct and the pre-R&D, post-depreciation margin is the right accounting fix, though the design is still the archive's standard "R&D intensity MIN gate" template and the margin leg is close to Novy-Marx gross profitability, so the incremental content is the accounting correction rather than a new channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Lifetime Research Payback in Retained Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: Within the R&D-intensity gate the ranking variable re/TS_SUM(xrd,5) is close to an inverse-R&D-intensity-times-retained-earnings composite, so it largely re-ranks the very characteristic the gate conditions on and overlaps the archived gen-0 Retained-Earnings-Financed Research Gate with only the denominator changed from assets to research spend.

critic_notes.target_name: Downside-Adjusted Cash Generation Behind Intangible-Light Firms
critic_notes.rationale: TS_MIN of a cash-flow series already impounds most of that series' volatility, so subtracting VOL from the floor is near-redundant arithmetic on two archived parents sharing an identical intangibles leg — the definition of a cosmetic variant, and the stated fallback ("we learn the floor already impounds stability") is an outcome that can be anticipated without the test.

critic_notes.target_name: Pre-Research Cash Return on Acquisitiveness-Penalized Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Adding R&D back to operating cash flow scaled by an asset base is essentially Ball-Gerakos-Linnainmaa-Nikolaev cash-based operating profitability (which explicitly adds back R&D), and the only differentiator from the archived gen-5 signal is the same double-counted-intangibles denominator, making this a known anomaly wearing a one-term modification.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-Year Pre-Research Return on Penalized Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Putting the five-year floor inside the ratio rather than conjoining two ranked legs is a genuinely different functional form with a coherent hypothesis, though it inherits the same pre-R&D cash-profitability numerator as the previous proposal and will remain coverage-constrained by the oancf history requirement.

critic_notes.target_name: Additive Composite of Intangible Lightness and Cash Floor
critic_notes.rationale: This is an explicit operator sweep over two legs already tested under MIN and MAX with no new economic content, and it is not even a clean comparison because the legs enter SUMRANK raw rather than industry-ranked, so any difference confounds functional form with the loss of industry adjustment.

critic_notes.target_name: Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
critic_notes.rationale: The buy-versus-build comparison of same-period flows is a construct the archive has not formed and the negative sign is consistent with the expression (high = acquisitive and cash-weak), though the Δ(goodwill+intangibles) leg overlaps materially with the well-documented asset-growth/acquisition anomaly and the long side of a MIN conjunction will be economically diffuse.

critic_notes.target_name: Income-Statement Cash Floor Behind Intangible-Light Firms
critic_notes.rationale: A proxy swap rather than a new mechanism, but the diagnosis is correct that oancf history is what binds coverage at 0.08–0.09 (ib-based five-year constructs reach 0.146), so this is a legitimate and decision-relevant robustness test of whether the archive's best result is a sample artefact.

critic_notes.target_name: Recent Deal Flow Versus Legacy Intangible Stock
critic_notes.rationale: The stock-versus-flow decomposition of the intangibles leg is a substantive and answerable question that the archive has not addressed, but note that TS_SUM(DELTA(x,1),5) telescopes to a plain five-year change in booked intangibles, which sits close to the published asset-growth and acquisitiveness anomalies and should be interpreted with that in mind.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Intangible Tilt with Claims-Coverage Floor
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical re-pairing of two already-tested legs ("Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Capital" and the oancf/(dlc+lct) worst-year coverage floor) whose only substantive change is dropping the redundant dlc from a denominator that already contains it, so it is a cosmetic variant highly likely to reproduce the archived 4.9% alpha rather than teach anything new.

critic_notes.target_name: Net Durable Intangible Capital Behind a Cash-Earnings Floor
critic_notes.rationale: Also a recombination of two archived legs, but the motivation is a genuine diagnostic (the netted-dollar construct has strong alpha with a flat FM slope, the cash-earnings floor the reverse) and it preserves the broad ~0.14 coverage instead of collapsing to the sparse oancf sample, so it is worth one test — though the two legs both embed debt and intangibles and may be too correlated to add much.

critic_notes.target_name: Self-Financed Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Once the telescoping TS_SUM of DELTA is unwound the expression is simply R&D intensity minus five-year net paid-in-capital growth, i.e. an additive blend of two well-known published anomalies (R&D intensity and net equity issuance/composite issuance) and a functional-form restatement of the archived gen-6 dilution signal, so a strong slope would be uninformative about anything new.

critic_notes.target_name: Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor
critic_notes.rationale: The horizon-mismatch critique is correct and the fix is internally consistent (TS_SUM of DELTA telescopes to a clean five-year change in booked intangibles), but the archive already showed flow and stock versions of the acquired-intangible penalty perform nearly identically (fmb 4.78 vs 4.59), so the expected incremental information is modest and partly overlaps known acquisition/asset-growth effects.

critic_notes.target_name: Research Alongside Retained Earnings Accumulation
critic_notes.rationale: This is the eleventh instance of the same template — MIN(R&D intensity, some ranked profitability leg) — and five-year Δre/at is close to cumulative ROA net of dividends, overlapping both the archived retained-earnings gate and the published retained-earnings/profitability literature, so it is too incremental to be worth a slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-Year Productivity of Knowledge-Augmented Capital
critic_notes.rationale: A single clean leg with no rank splice that applies a specific, previously informative transformation (the five-year floor) to an intangible-augmented cash gross profitability ratio; it overlaps gross profitability and intangible-adjusted-capital literature and the archived penalized-capital floor, but the income-statement construction, broader coverage, and the level-vs-floor diagnostic make it a substantive rather than cosmetic test.

critic_notes.target_name: Consolidated Net Durable Intangible Capital with Cash-Earnings Floor
critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archived gen-7 "Net Durable Intangible Capital Behind a Cash-Earnings Floor," differing only in swapping the stock of purchased intangibles for its five-year flow (a change already tested in the gen-7 build-minus-buy signal), so it is a mechanical recombination of validated parts rather than a new economic mechanism, and the arbitrary dollar-for-dollar netting of dlc against R&D remains unmotivated.

critic_notes.target_name: Research Intensity with Cash-Denominated Deal Premium
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnosis (zero FMB slope from compression near zero) is sensible and the pairing is new, but the second leg is numerically fragile because TS_SUM(oancf,5) can be negative or near-offsetting, making the ratio non-monotone and capable of ranking distressed cash-burners at the top — precisely the population the R&D-intensity leg selects — so the conjunction may amplify rather than fix the leg's defect.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquisitive Expansion Without an Earnings Floor
critic_notes.rationale: The joint-failure corner (heavy five-year intangible build plus no cash-earnings floor) is a genuinely different quadrant from the archived gen-6 "Recent Deal Flow" positive-corner signal and the sign is internally consistent with the MIN construction, though both legs individually are close to the well-known asset-growth and profitability anomalies, so incremental content over a simple asset-growth/profitability double sort is uncertain.

critic_notes.target_name: Freshness of the Knowledge Stock
critic_notes.rationale: Vintage of the knowledge stock is the one dimension the archive has never measured and the ratio is cleanly self-normalising, but the reviewer should note it is close to the published R&D-increase anomaly (Eberhart–Maxwell–Siddique) and that 0.05 coverage plus a mechanically bounded denominator will limit dispersion, so treat a strong result with appropriate caution.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquisitiveness Penalty Alone at Full Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archived gen-6 "Recent Deal Flow Versus Legacy Intangible Stock" with the oancf floor swapped for the ib+dp floor already validated in gen-6, i.e. two archived components joined by a substitution whose effect is known, so the ablation is only weakly informative and near-certain to reproduce prior results.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-Year Cash Earnings on Penalized Capital at Full Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: A one-input proxy swap (oancf → ib+dp) on the archived gen-6 "Worst-Year Pre-Research Return on Penalized Capital" is exactly the cosmetic coverage-extension variant the objective warns against, and the double-charging of goodwill in the denominator is an arbitrary weighting inherited unexamined from the parent.

critic_notes.target_name: Horizon-Matched Build Minus Buy with Claims-Coverage Floor
critic_notes.rationale: Internally coherent but essentially a mechanical re-pairing of two already-tested legs, with the gate swapped from a worst-year oancf/at floor to a near-collinear oancf/lct floor, so it is very likely a high-correlation near-duplicate of the gen-7 "Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor" rather than a substantively new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale
critic_notes.rationale: A denominator change is a modest edit, but the stated purpose—testing whether the repeated build-minus-buy result is an asset-lightness/capital-intensity artefact rather than an allocation effect—is a legitimate identification test with a clear diagnostic payoff, and the expression matches the hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit-Funded Knowledge Stock
critic_notes.rationale: The construction genuinely embeds the earnings condition inside the accumulation in a way no archive leg does and the sign logic is consistent, but it sits close to the well-known R&D-capital-to-assets anomaly and will be highly correlated with the plain TS_SUM(xrd,5)/at leg since most firm-years are profitable, so the incremental content may be small.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit-Funded Knowledge Net of Deal Outlays
critic_notes.rationale: This is the previous proposal spliced onto the archive's already-tested "Net Durable Intangible Capital"/build-minus-buy numerator, so it is an incremental composite whose only new element is the profit indicator, and it imposes an arbitrary unit-for-unit netting of two heterogeneous dollar flows without justification.

critic_notes.target_name: Deal Outlays and Near-Term Debt Against the Equity Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: Dividing by book equity (at − lt) is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis because negative- or near-zero-equity firms—exactly the fragile cases the signal claims to identify—produce large negative or exploding ratios that rank as safest, and 1% winsorisation does not repair the sign flip.

critic_notes.target_name: Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent conditional pairing that extends the industry-relative floor to the larger income-statement sample, though the claimed resolution of the moat-versus-industry-composition question is overstated since the outer IND_RANK already removes industry level and only the within-window ordering of the demeaned series adds new information.

validation_diagnostics.message: proposal expression does not use any variable exclusive to required theme: quality (variables shared across the paired themes, e.g. common denominators like 'at', do not count as evidence for either theme)
